source_state: Observer deadline, submitted-work maintenance and v4 consumer changes were uncommitted during measurement; the report records their qualified revisions after commit.

environment.NARA_RUNTIME_COST_OUTPUT: An explicit absolute new temporary JSON file, separate from ordinary startup stdout and stderr.

workload.idle_caller_wait_cap: Remaining requested interval, not an independent 2 ms cap.
workload.order: Condition order reverses on alternating runs; plain/witness order independently alternates by pair.

deadline_control.arming: Original zero-wait native maintenance publishes the request before allowing the long native wait.

workload.acceptance: Both Wait conditions reduce aggregate App frames by at least 80 percent; no-deadline Wait reduces observer callbacks and native poll calls by at least 90 percent versus periodic Wait. Complete canonical bytes, zero paused simulation/logical ticks, explicit maintenance/Step/Resume/Pause and all original telemetry/native cleanup remain required.

limits: This is a matched three-condition comparison within one maintained implementation, not a controlled binary comparison with the historical v3 run.
Sequential native runs share process code, driver allocations and caches; they are not independent cold starts.
Cooperative Poll intervals last about 332-333 ms and both Wait intervals about 300 ms; actual wall spans remain in the raw record.
Two observer callbacks per single no-deadline native poll reflect the original Windows pump boundaries, not periodic 2 ms wakeups.
Process CPU is separately sampled, quantized and variable; callback/poll counts do not establish stable CPU, power, GPU execution, scanout or tail budgets.
The consumer proves explicit observer and known pending-submission maintenance, not automatic wakes from arbitrary task, World or cache-lifetime changes.
The 250 ms observation gate is cooperative and cannot interrupt callbacks, drivers or native APIs.
Native Windows/DX12 on the reported hardware is qualified; foreign execution remains open.
